library_preparation_preflight.summary: No extra Maven dependency, Docker image, or external service is needed. Meaningful JLine/TUI coverage should use an in-memory dumb terminal fixture; the published POM already supplies the required runtime APIs ([POM](https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/springframework/shell/spring-shell-jline/4.0.2/spring-shell-jline-4.0.2.pom)).
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Construct org.jline.terminal.impl.DumbTerminal with byte-array or piped streams and a fixed terminal size, then use it with LineReaderBuilder, JLineInputReader, ComponentFlow, TUI components, styling, completion, and table APIs. Clean up terminals and helper threads. Avoid relying on a real TTY or default native provider selection. If testing DefaultJLineShellConfiguration.terminal(), set org.jline.terminal.provider=dumb before terminal creation. Follow the upstream fixture pattern ([upstream tests](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-shell/tree/v4.0.2/spring-shell-jline/src/test/java/org/springframework/shell/jline)).
risks: Default TerminalBuilder behavior may probe FFM, JNI, Jansi, JNA, or exec providers and be platform-dependent; local Native Image verification remains authoritative.

Spring Boot auto-configuration belongs to Spring Shell Core Autoconfigure; do not add it solely for direct spring-shell-jline API coverage ([documentation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-shell/reference/building.html)).
